# Welcome to Beyond, the Plant Protein Company

[Scroll to See How][2]

## Beyond The Plant Protein Company committed to everyday nourishment.

## Simple, clean ingredients

Meet our line-up. Food you can feel good about, bite after bite:
* Plant proteins sourced from ingredients like yellow peas, red lentils, and faba beans
* No GMOs, 0mg cholesterol, and no added hormones or antibiotics

[Discover Products][3][Store Locator][4]
[Beyond Burger]

### Beyond Burger

Beyond burgers are the perfect blend of comfort food and clean eating with ingredients you can read
like avocado oil.

21g Protein
2g Saturated Fat
0mg Cholesterol

Nutritional info per 1 patty

[Product Details][5][WHERE TO BUY][6]
[Beyond Steak Tips]

### Beyond Steak Tips

Beyond Steak Tips add some rich and savory sizzle to your fajitas, stir fries, and salads.

21g Protein
1g Saturated Fat
170 Calories

Nutritional info per 3/4 cup steak tips

[Product Details][7][WHERE TO BUY][8]
[Beyond Chicken Pieces]

### Beyond Chicken Pieces

Beyond Chicken is clean protein reimagined— juicy, versatile, and air-fryer ready.

21g Protein
0.5g Saturated Fat
130 Calories

Nutritional info per 3/4 cup chicken pieces

[Product Details][9][WHERE TO BUY][10]
[Beyond Beef]

### Beyond Beef

Beyond Beef is the protein you can build any meal around, whether it’s tacos, pasta, or a protein
bowl.

21g Protein
2g Saturated Fat
230 Calories

Nutritional info per 4oz ground

[Product Details][11][WHERE TO BUY][12]
[Beyond Sausage]

### Beyond Sausage

Beyond Sausage is a mouth-watering addition to pasta, stir-fry, or just grilled with a bun.

17g Protein
0mg Cholesterol
210 Calories

Nutritional info per 1 link

[Product Details][13][WHERE TO BUY][14]
[Discover Products][15][Store Locator][16]
123

## Plants are nutrition powerhouses.

Our team is dedicated to unlocking and delivering nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, and healthy
fats.

[Learn More][17]

## Plants are nutrition powerhouses.

Our team is dedicated to unlocking and delivering nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, and healthy
fats.

[Learn More][18]

## We love clean protein.

Our products are full of powerful plant protein, with no added hormones, antibiotics, GMOs, or
cholesterol.

[Learn More][19]

## We believe in plant fiber.

Our products also include dietary fiber, essential fuel for the gut microbiome.

[Learn More][20]
[Plants are nutrition powerhouses.]

## Starting back at the farm

Meet Steven, a 5th generation farmer and father in Munich, North Dakota. He grows faba beans for
Beyond, a soil-enriching crop that helps regenerate farmland naturally. Stephen’s faba beans are one
of the simple, non-GMO ingredients that help Beyond bring you clean, wholesome plant protein that’s
good for the planet and your diet.

[Learn More][21]
[No Cholesterol;Faba bean protein;Avocado Oil;Simple ingredients;No antibiotics or hormones]

## Feeding a better future

We create plant protein to nourish and protect our bodies, heal earth and climate, and better share
the planet with the miracle of life that surrounds us.

[Our Mission][22]
[Feeding a better future]

## See what we’re cooking up next

Beyond Test Kitchen is where our newest ideas come to life, and where you come in. What excites us
most is creating products that bring energy and joy to our families, friends, and community. Beyond
Test Kitchen is our open innovation platform where you get early access to upcoming launches and
help shape what comes next.

[Shop Now][23]
[Chef holding a plate of two Beyond Steaks with asparagus and potatoes.]

Join the Evolution

Sign up for our mailing list for early access to new products, exclusive discounts, Beyond The Plant
Protein Company news, and more.

By clicking 'Sign Up', you consent to Beyond Meat® using your email address in accordance with its
[Privacy Policy][24]. You can opt-out at any time.

### about us

## We are committed to shaping the future of plant-based foods.

Our portfolio of leading plant-based protein brands includes Lightlife® and Field Roast™.

### our brands

## Meet Our Plant-Based Brands

[ll_logo_primary_tagline_rgb][ll_logo_primary_tagline_rgb]

A pioneer in the plant-based foods movement for over 40 years, Lightlife® has a wide portfolio of
plant-based protein products and is proud to make the #1 brand of tempeh and the #1 plant-based hot
dog in the U.S. In 2018, Lightlife® expanded into Canada, bringing its bestselling products to that
market.

#### [Visit Site >][12]

[fieldroast_logo_rgb_bil][fieldroast_logo_rgb_bil]

Field Roast™ crafts artisanal plant-based meats and cheeses, made with whole food ingredients and
traditional food-making practices. Founded in 1997, its ever-expanding product portfolio includes
sausages, roasts, loaves, deli slices, a burger, and plant-based cheese slices and shreds

Our portfolio of leading plant-based protein brands includes Lightlife® and Field Roast™.

### our brands

plant-based protein products and is proud to make the #1 brand of tempeh and the #1 plant-based hot

market.

## OurMission

big change

We strive to make delicious food that’s nutritious, better for the planet, and way better for
animals. "The way to solve the most important and urgent problem humanity has potentially ever faced
turned out to be to figure out how to make the best burger on earth."

Pat Brown, Founder of Impossible Foods

Nutrient-packedBetter for the PlanetWay better for AnimalsQuality Ingredients

We are all about making unbelievably tasty meats that are a nutritious, healthy alternative to the
animal version—like our heart-healthy¹ Lite Ground Beef.

Our delicious products are nutrient-packed and have 0 mg cholesterol.² And our super meaty beef that
made us kind of famous has 19 g protein/serving and 33% less fat than the animal version.² Aren't
plants amazing?

¹ Diets low in saturated fat and cholesterol, and as low as possible in trans fat, may reduce the
risk of heart disease.
² Saturated fat per serving: USDA 80/20 animal ground beef 9g; Impossible Beef 6g.
[Lite Ground Beef][50]

Animal agriculture's global greenhouse gas footprint is even more massive than that of the global
transportation sector—which is every car, ship, plane, and rocket ship on Earth... combined.. Yep,
combined.

Luckily, we live in a time in history when animals are not the only way to produce everybody's
favorite food. Simply choosing Impossible Beef over the animal version uses approximately 96% less
land and 92% less water, while generating 91% less greenhouse gases.
[Our Mission][51]

Everyone loves meat because it's so craveably delicious. Not because it comes from animals — who
even wants to think about that part?

Planet of the Cows? 45% of the Earth's land is being used to either raise cows or grow food to feed
cows*—all on land that was once wildlife habitat. Newsflash: the cows aren't enjoying it either. By
replacing animals in the food system with meat from plants, massive amounts of land and water can be
spared for biodiversity and wildlife, not to mention the lives of chickens, cows and pigs.

*Based on a Nov 2011 study by the International Livestock Research Institute
[More about our mission][52]
[Image not found]

Our products are made from plants. You know, grown on farms from the soil of the Earth, cooled by
rain and warmed by the sun.

The copywriter isn't trying to be poetic, that's just how plants work. We source 99% of the soy in
Impossible Beef from lovely American farms.
[Check Out Our Awesome Ingredients ][53]

## Browse ourFAQ's

We've got answers to the most common questions about our products, preparation methods, nutrition –
you name it.

### What Are the Ingredients in Impossible™ Beef Meat From Plants?

Impossible® Beef is a mix of proteins, flavors, fats, and binders. The key difference from your
average beef from animals? Our ingredients are derived from plants. Here's an overview:
* Protein from soy
* Flavor from heme (the molecule that makes meat taste, well, meaty)
* Fat from sunflower and coconut oils makes it sizzle on the griddle
* Binders hold it together so you can make anything you want — meatballs, kebabs, patties, and more.

Want the details? [Click here.][54]

### What Are the Nutrition Facts for Impossible™ Beef Meat From Plants?

Here for quick answers? Cool. Every 4 oz. serving of Impossible® Beef contains:
* 19g protein (the same as 80/20 ground beef)
* 0mg cholesterol (6g saturated fat)
* 25% the daily value of iron
* No antibiotics or animal hormones

Looking for more details? Also cool. Click [here][55].

[Click here][56]

### Do your products contain gluten?

Impossible® Steak Bites Meat From Plants, Impossible® Beef Meat From Plants, Impossible® Sausage
Meat From Plants, Impossible® Meatballs Meat From Plants, and Impossible® Pork Meat From Plants have
no gluten-containing ingredients. Impossible® Chicken Nuggets Meat From Plants, Patties, Tenders, as
well as Impossible® Beef Hot Dogs Meat From Plants do contain gluten. We encourage you to review our
ingredient labels regularly, as we are continually working to improve the taste and nutrition of
Impossible® products, including through periodic recipe updates. If you're dining out, please apply
the same level of caution that you would with any food and check with the restaurant about
cross-contamination risks. Please also note that some products (like Impossible® Bowls) contain
ingredients in addition to Impossible meat made from plants. If you have food allergies or
sensitivities, please take extra care in reviewing these products’ ingredient lists in their
entirety. Want the details? Click [here][57].

## OurMission

big change

We strive to make delicious food that’s nutritious, better for the planet, and way better for
animals. "The way to solve the most important and urgent problem humanity has potentially ever faced
turned out to be to figure out how to make the best burger on earth."

Pat Brown, Founder of Impossible Foods

Nutrient-packedBetter for the PlanetWay better for AnimalsQuality Ingredients

We are all about making unbelievably tasty meats that are a nutritious, healthy alternative to the
animal version—like our heart-healthy¹ Lite Ground Beef.

Our delicious products are nutrient-packed and have 0 mg cholesterol.² And our super meaty beef that
made us kind of famous has 19 g protein/serving and 33% less fat than the animal version.² Aren't
plants amazing?

¹ Diets low in saturated fat and cholesterol, and as low as possible in trans fat, may reduce the
risk of heart disease.
² Saturated fat per serving: USDA 80/20 animal ground beef 9g; Impossible Beef 6g.
[Lite Ground Beef][50]

Animal agriculture's global greenhouse gas footprint is even more massive than that of the global
transportation sector—which is every car, ship, plane, and rocket ship on Earth... combined.. Yep,
combined.

Luckily, we live in a time in history when animals are not the only way to produce everybody's
favorite food. Simply choosing Impossible Beef over the animal version uses approximately 96% less
land and 92% less water, while generating 91% less greenhouse gases.
[Our Mission][51]

Everyone loves meat because it's so craveably delicious. Not because it comes from animals — who
even wants to think about that part?

Planet of the Cows? 45% of the Earth's land is being used to either raise cows or grow food to feed
cows*—all on land that was once wildlife habitat. Newsflash: the cows aren't enjoying it either. By
replacing animals in the food system with meat from plants, massive amounts of land and water can be
spared for biodiversity and wildlife, not to mention the lives of chickens, cows and pigs.

*Based on a Nov 2011 study by the International Livestock Research Institute
[More about our mission][52]
[Image not found]

Our products are made from plants. You know, grown on farms from the soil of the Earth, cooled by
rain and warmed by the sun.

The copywriter isn't trying to be poetic, that's just how plants work. We source 99% of the soy in
Impossible Beef from lovely American farms.
[Check Out Our Awesome Ingredients ][53]

## Browse ourFAQ's

We've got answers to the most common questions about our products, preparation methods, nutrition –
you name it.

### What Are the Ingredients in Impossible™ Beef Meat From Plants?

Impossible® Beef is a mix of proteins, flavors, fats, and binders. The key difference from your
average beef from animals? Our ingredients are derived from plants. Here's an overview:
* Protein from soy
* Flavor from heme (the molecule that makes meat taste, well, meaty)
* Fat from sunflower and coconut oils makes it sizzle on the griddle
* Binders hold it together so you can make anything you want — meatballs, kebabs, patties, and more.

Want the details? [Click here.][54]

### What Are the Nutrition Facts for Impossible™ Beef Meat From Plants?

Here for quick answers? Cool. Every 4 oz. serving of Impossible® Beef contains:
* 19g protein (the same as 80/20 ground beef)
* 0mg cholesterol (6g saturated fat)
* 25% the daily value of iron
* No antibiotics or animal hormones

Looking for more details? Also cool. Click [here][55].

[Click here][56]

### Do your products contain gluten?

Impossible® Steak Bites Meat From Plants, Impossible® Beef Meat From Plants, Impossible® Sausage
Meat From Plants, Impossible® Meatballs Meat From Plants, and Impossible® Pork Meat From Plants have
no gluten-containing ingredients. Impossible® Chicken Nuggets Meat From Plants, Patties, Tenders, as
well as Impossible® Beef Hot Dogs Meat From Plants do contain gluten. We encourage you to review our
ingredient labels regularly, as we are continually working to improve the taste and nutrition of
Impossible® products, including through periodic recipe updates. If you're dining out, please apply
the same level of caution that you would with any food and check with the restaurant about
cross-contamination risks. Please also note that some products (like Impossible® Bowls) contain
ingredients in addition to Impossible meat made from plants. If you have food allergies or
sensitivities, please take extra care in reviewing these products’ ingredient lists in their
entirety. Want the details? Click [here][57].

How it’s made, starring MrBeast:

## It all starts with a single egg.

8 years ago, UPSIDE took cells from a heritage breed chicken egg. Those cells form a master cell
bank from which UPSIDE can make millions of pounds of cultivated chicken.

## Same cells, same feed, different body.

UPSIDE feeds the cells the same vitamins, minerals and nutrients they’d get from chicken feed. The
only difference is the vessel. UPSIDE chicken is grown in tanks (like you’d see at a brewery)
instead of inside a chicken.

## In just 3 weeks, those cells become UPSIDE chicken.

## FAQs
* Real chicken without animals?! Then how the cluck is UPSIDE chicken made?
  
  We’re so glad you asked, but watch your language please, our boss goes to this site. Yes, UPSIDE
  chicken is real chicken, made without killing countless animals or factory farming.
  
  How?
  
  Our process starts with cell samples from one, single heritage-breed chicken egg. That sample is
  stored and can be used for years. (In fact, all the chicken we’ve ever manufactured came from one
  single egg. Pretty cool, huh?)
  
  We select the best cells from that sample and place them in a cultivator–a tank similar to what
  you’d find in a brewery. The cells are fed a nutrient-rich blend of water, sugars, amino acids,
  vitamins and minerals–the same kind of nutrients free-range chickens get from their feed.
  
  After a few weeks, the cultivated chicken is supercharged with plants and ready to star in all
  your favorite chicken dishes!
* What measures do you take to ensure your meat is safe?
  
  Great question! It’s our mission to make meat right, and a huge part of that is safety. We undergo
  double the regulatory scrutiny of conventional meat (both the FDA and USDA have to give us the
  green light to sell our cultivated meat). Additionally, UPSIDE chicken is made in a pristine
  environment–a far cry from factory farms–which keeps our chicken safe from foodborne illnesses
  like salmonella and bird flu.
  
  For more on how cultivated meat is regulated, check out this [FDA explainer][16].
* What are the environmental benefits of cultivated meat?
  
  Several independent researchers have published life cycle analyses projecting the impact of
  cultivated meat will be significantly less than conventional animal agriculture as its production
  scales. One study from The Good Food Institute, for instance, finds that cultivated meat may
  require up to 90% less land and water and emit up to 90% fewer greenhouse gasses. As we scale up
  our manufacturing, we’re working hard to make this future a reality.
* What are the ingredients in UPSIDE chicken?
  
  Here are the main stars of the show:
  
  Water: You’re probably familiar with this one.
  
  Cell Cultivated Chicken: The star of the show, grown in a pristine, controlled environment.
  
  Soy Protein Isolate: A concentrated, complete (contains all nine essential amino acids) protein.
  
  Pea Fiber: A source of essential dietary fiber.
  
  Avocado Oil: A wholesome oil extracted from avocados, rich in monounsaturated fatty acids.
  
  Here’s the full ingredient list:
  Water, Cell Cultivated Chicken, Soy Protein Isolate, Pea Fiber, Avocado Oil, Contains less than 2%
  of: Soy Lecithin, Glutamic Acid, Onion Powder, Salt, Garlic Powder, Yeast Extract, Natural
  Flavors, Sugar, Pea Protein, Dried Citrus Pulp, Citric Acid, Tartaric Acid. *Ingredients subject
  to change.
* What if I have infrequently asked questions? Where do I ask those? Tell me everything!
  
  We love talking about cultivated meat. And to “cultivate” more conversation (ba dum tss), we made
  Stan, our educational agent that we trained on all things UPSIDE! Ask a question [here][17]
  anytime.
* Is UPSIDE chicken vegetarian?
  
  UPSIDE chicken is not vegetarian or vegan—it’s actual meat, made from real chicken cells. However,
  there’s a big difference between UPSIDE and conventional chicken: since UPSIDE chicken is made
  from cells, there’s no need to raise and kill animals to enjoy it.
  
  Tl;dr: if you love the taste of chicken but avoid meat for ethical reasons, UPSIDE gives you a new
  option. Our chicken lets you enjoy the delicious taste of real meat, without all the icks of
  factory farming.

  chicken is real chicken, made without killing countless animals or factory farming.
  
  How?
  
  Our process starts with cell samples from one, single heritage-breed chicken egg. That sample is
  stored and can be used for years. (In fact, all the chicken we’ve ever manufactured came from one
  single egg. Pretty cool, huh?)
  
  We select the best cells from that sample and place them in a cultivator–a tank similar to what
  you’d find in a brewery. The cells are fed a nutrient-rich blend of water, sugars, amino acids,
  vitamins and minerals–the same kind of nutrients free-range chickens get from their feed.
  
  After a few weeks, the cultivated chicken is supercharged with plants and ready to star in all
  your favorite chicken dishes!
* What measures do you take to ensure your meat is safe?
  
  Great question! It’s our mission to make meat right, and a huge part of that is safety. We undergo
  double the regulatory scrutiny of conventional meat (both the FDA and USDA have to give us the
  green light to sell our cultivated meat). Additionally, UPSIDE chicken is made in a pristine
  environment–a far cry from factory farms–which keeps our chicken safe from foodborne illnesses
  like salmonella and bird flu.
  
  For more on how cultivated meat is regulated, check out this [FDA explainer][16].
* What are the environmental benefits of cultivated meat?
  
  Several independent researchers have published life cycle analyses projecting the impact of
  cultivated meat will be significantly less than conventional animal agriculture as its production
  scales. One study from The Good Food Institute, for instance, finds that cultivated meat may
  require up to 90% less land and water and emit up to 90% fewer greenhouse gasses. As we scale up
  our manufacturing, we’re working hard to make this future a reality.
* What are the ingredients in UPSIDE chicken?
  
  Here are the main stars of the show:
  
  Water: You’re probably familiar with this one.
  
  Cell Cultivated Chicken: The star of the show, grown in a pristine, controlled environment.
  
  Soy Protein Isolate: A concentrated, complete (contains all nine essential amino acids) protein.
  
  Pea Fiber: A source of essential dietary fiber.
  
  Avocado Oil: A wholesome oil extracted from avocados, rich in monounsaturated fatty acids.
  
  Here’s the full ingredient list:
  Water, Cell Cultivated Chicken, Soy Protein Isolate, Pea Fiber, Avocado Oil, Contains less than 2%
  of: Soy Lecithin, Glutamic Acid, Onion Powder, Salt, Garlic Powder, Yeast Extract, Natural
  Flavors, Sugar, Pea Protein, Dried Citrus Pulp, Citric Acid, Tartaric Acid. *Ingredients subject
  to change.
* What if I have infrequently asked questions? Where do I ask those? Tell me everything!
  
  We love talking about cultivated meat. And to “cultivate” more conversation (ba dum tss), we made
  Stan, our educational agent that we trained on all things UPSIDE! Ask a question [here][17]
  anytime.
* Is UPSIDE chicken vegetarian?
  
  UPSIDE chicken is not vegetarian or vegan—it’s actual meat, made from real chicken cells. However,
  there’s a big difference between UPSIDE and conventional chicken: since UPSIDE chicken is made
  from cells, there’s no need to raise and kill animals to enjoy it.
  
  Tl;dr: if you love the taste of chicken but avoid meat for ethical reasons, UPSIDE gives you a new
  option. Our chicken lets you enjoy the delicious taste of real meat, without all the icks of
  factory farming.
* Can UPSIDE make other types of meat too?
  
  Yes! The innovative process we’ve created to cultivate chicken can work with all types of meats –
  we’re talking meat, poultry, and even seafood! We are always working on new products so in the
  future we’ll be able to satisfy all different kinds of meaty cravings.
* How much does UPSIDE chicken cost?
  
  UPSIDE chicken is currently exclusively available to the public through our amazing restaurant
  partners. While they set the ultimate prices for their menu, we’re working hard to scale up
  production so we can offer UPSIDE chicken at everyday prices. It’s our goal to expand cultivated
  meat beyond fine dining and make it accessible to everyone.

  We believe in a future with more options for consumers, including the option to choose how the
  protein on your plate is made – whether conventional meat, cultivated meat or plant-based meat.
  
  This will be especially important in the near future, as demand for meat is expected to double by
  2050, and there just aren’t enough resources for the conventional meat industry to meet that kind
  of demand. We see cultivated meat as a way to close that supply gap and give people the meat they
  want.

  We can’t wait for you to try what we’ve been cooking up! Stay tuned for announcements about new
  products and locations soon.

## Pioneering a cleaner, kinder way of making beef.

We’re Mosa Meat, a food technology company that’s helping everyone take a bite out of a better
future – starting with the world’s kindest beef burger.

### News: Mosa Meat Secures Additional €15M in Funding & Reaches Cost Parity Milestone

[ Read more… ][20]
 
 

### Crave change?

## We want to introduce a new way of thinking about, growing, making, and enjoying food.

## A next step which is kinder for all of us – and the planet – but doesn’t mean sacrificing taste.

[ Check out our mission ][21]

## Feel good indulgence

 We’re making the beef burgers of the future.

They don’t taste ‘just like’ meat. They are real meat. Real beef that oozes and sizzles with real
fats and juices.

We’re making these burgers so people can make a positive impact on the planet, simply by swapping
delicious beef… with delicious beef. Easy!

## How do we do it?
## With science, naturally.

[cow01.jpg]
 

We grow our beef by harnessing the same natural processes responsible for muscle growth in a cow.

We start by taking a sesame-seed sized sample of cells, and nurturing them to naturally grow into
beef. We can make up to 80,000 burgers just from that one sample – and no animal is harmed.

And just like a farmer cares for their herd, we give the same care and attention to every cell.

## Technologies

Explore the cutting-edge technologies driving the future of protein production.

[
[Plant-Based Proteins]

### Plant-Based Proteins

Plant-based proteins are derived from various plant sources like soy, peas, wheat, and rice. They
are processed using extrusion technology to mimic the texture and taste of conventional meat
products. The global plant-based protein market has seen explosive growth, driven by consumer demand
for sustainable and healthier food options. Modern extrusion processes use moisture, high heat, and
mechanical energy to transform plant protein powders into meat substitutes with remarkably similar
texture profiles to animal protein.

Learn More
][12]

[Precision Fermentation]

### Precision Fermentation

Precision fermentation uses genetically engineered microorganisms to produce specific organic
molecules such as proteins, fats, and vitamins. By programming microbes to act as miniature
factories, this technology can create animal-free versions of dairy proteins, collagen, heme, and
other complex molecules. It represents one of the most promising approaches for creating identical
molecular copies of animal-derived ingredients without any animal involvement.

[
[Biomass Fermentation]

### Biomass Fermentation

Biomass fermentation utilizes the rapid growth of microorganisms to produce large quantities of
protein-rich biomass. Unlike precision fermentation, the entire microorganism is harvested and
processed, making it a highly efficient method for generating protein at scale. This approach
leverages fungi, bacteria, and yeast to convert simple sugars and other feedstocks into nutritious,
high-protein food ingredients.

Learn More
][14]
[
[Cultivated Meat]

### Cultivated Meat

Cultivated meat (also known as cell-cultured meat or lab-grown meat) is genuine animal meat produced
by cultivating animal cells in a controlled environment. This technology eliminates the need to
raise and slaughter animals, offering a more sustainable and ethical approach to meat production.
The process involves taking a small sample of cells and growing them in a nutrient-rich medium
within bioreactors, creating real animal tissue.

Learn More
][15]
[
[Insect Protein]

### Insect Protein

Insect protein is derived from the farming and processing of various insect species, primarily black
soldier fly larvae, mealworms, and crickets. Insects are one of the most resource-efficient protein
sources on the planet, requiring significantly less land, water, and feed compared to conventional
livestock. The industry is rapidly scaling with automated farming systems and advanced processing
technologies.

Learn More
][16]
[
[Mycoprotein]

### Mycoprotein

Mycoprotein is a protein-rich food source made from naturally occurring fungi, primarily Fusarium
venenatum. It is produced through biomass fermentation where the fungus is grown continuously in
large fermenters. Mycoprotein has a naturally fibrous structure that closely mimics the texture of
meat, making it an excellent base for meat alternatives. It is high in protein, low in fat, and
contains all essential amino acids.

Learn More
][17]
[
[Algae Protein]

### Algae Protein

organisms on Earth. Microalgae like Spirulina and Chlorella have been consumed for centuries and
contain 50-70% protein by dry weight. Modern cultivation systems using photobioreactors and open
ponds enable large-scale production of algal biomass for food, feed, and nutraceutical applications.

][18]

[Hybrid Systems]

### Hybrid Systems

leverage the strengths of each technology. For example, combining plant-based textures with
precision fermentation-derived fats and flavors, or blending cultivated meat cells with plant-based
scaffolds. These integrated approaches aim to deliver superior taste, texture, nutrition, and cost
efficiency compared to single-technology solutions.

cultivation. This includes establishing primary cell cultures from tissue biopsies, developing
stable cell lines that can proliferate indefinitely

## Technologies

Explore the cutting-edge technologies driving the future of protein production.

[
[Plant-Based Proteins]

### Plant-Based Proteins

Plant-based proteins are derived from various plant sources like soy, peas, wheat, and rice. They
are processed using extrusion technology to mimic the texture and taste of conventional meat
products. The global plant-based protein market has seen explosive growth, driven by consumer demand
for sustainable and healthier food options. Modern extrusion processes use moisture, high heat, and
mechanical energy to transform plant protein powders into meat substitutes with remarkably similar
texture profiles to animal protein.

Learn More
][12]
[
[Precision Fermentation]

### Precision Fermentation

Precision fermentation uses genetically engineered microorganisms to produce specific organic
molecules such as proteins, fats, and vitamins. By programming microbes to act as miniature
factories, this technology can create animal-free versions of dairy proteins, collagen, heme, and
other complex molecules. It represents one of the most promising approaches for creating identical
molecular copies of animal-derived ingredients without any animal involvement.

Learn More
][13]
[
[Biomass Fermentation]

### Biomass Fermentation

Biomass fermentation utilizes the rapid growth of microorganisms to produce large quantities of
protein-rich biomass. Unlike precision fermentation, the entire microorganism is harvested and
processed, making it a highly efficient method for generating protein at scale. This approach
leverages fungi, bacteria, and yeast to convert simple sugars and other feedstocks into nutritious,
high-protein food ingredients.

Learn More

by cultivating animal cells in a controlled environment. This technology eliminates the need to
raise and slaughter animals, offering a more sustainable and ethical approach to meat production.
The process involves taking a small sample of cells and growing them in a nutrient-rich medium
within bioreactors, creating real animal tissue.

Learn More

[
[Insect Protein]

### Insect Protein

soldier fly larvae, mealworms, and crickets. Insects are one of the most resource-efficient protein
sources on the planet, requiring significantly less land, water, and feed compared to conventional
livestock. The industry is rapidly scaling with automated farming systems and advanced processing
technologies.

Learn More
][16]
[
[Mycoprotein]

### Mycoprotein

venenatum. It is produced through biomass fermentation where the fungus is grown continuously in
large fermenters. Mycoprotein has a naturally fibrous structure that closely mimics the texture of
meat, making it an excellent base for meat alternatives. It is high in protein, low in fat, and
contains all essential amino acids.

Learn More
][17]
[
[Algae Protein]

### Algae Protein

Algae protein is derived from microalgae and macroalgae (seaweed), some of the fastest-growing
organisms on Earth. Microalgae like Spirulina and Chlorella have been consumed for centuries and
contain 50-70% protein by dry weight. Modern cultivation systems using photobioreactors and open

Learn More
][18]
[
[Hybrid Systems]

### Hybrid Systems

Hybrid systems combine two or more alternative protein production methods to create products that
leverage the strengths of each technology. For example, combining plant-based textures with
precision fermentation-derived fats and flavors, or blending cultivated meat cells with plant-based
scaffolds. These integrated approaches aim to deliver superior taste, texture, nutrition, and cost
efficiency compared to single-technology solutions.

Learn More
][19]
[
[Cell Line Development]

### Cell Line Development

Cell line development is the foundational process for cultivated meat production, involving the
isolation, characterization, and immortalization of animal cells suitable for large-scale
cultivation. This includes establishing primary cell cultures from tissue biopsies, developing
stable cell lines that can proliferate indefinitely, and optimizing cell characteristics for food
production such as growth rate, differentiation capacity, and nutritional profile.

Learn More
][20]
[
[Protein Texturization]

### Protein Texturization

Protein texturization encompasses a range of technologies that convert protein isolates and
concentrates into fibrous, meat-like structures. Methods include high-moisture extrusion (HME),
low-moisture extrusion (TVP), shear cell technology, and electrospinning. These processes manipulate
protein molecules through heat, pressure, and shear forces to create the fibrous architecture found
in animal muscle tissue.

Learn More
][21]
[
[Growth Media Technologies]

### Growth Media Technologies

Growth media technologies focus on developing cost-effective, animal-free nutrient solutions that
support cell growth and proliferation in cultivated meat and precision fermentation processes. The
media is the single largest cost driver in cell culture, and innovations in serum-free,
chemically-defined, and plant-based media formulations are critical to making cultivated products
economically viable.

Learn More
][22]
[
[Scaffold Technologies]

### Scaffold Technologies

Scaffold technologies provide the three-dimensional structural framework that enables cultivated
meat cells to organize into tissue-like architectures. Scaffolds mimic the extracellular matrix of
animal tissues, guiding cell attachment, proliferation, and differentiation. Materials range from
plant-based proteins and polysaccharides to synthetic polymers and decellularized plant structures.

Learn More
][23]
[
[Downstream Processing]

### Downstream Processing

Downstream processing encompasses all the unit operations required to recover, purify, and formulate
the target product from fermentation broth or cell culture. In the alternative protein industry,
this includes cell harvesting, lysis, filtration, chromatography, concentration, and drying.
Efficient downstream processing is crucial for product quality and cost-effectiveness.

Learn More
][24]
[
[Separation & Purification]

### Separation & Purification

Separation and purification technologies are specialized unit operations that isolate target
molecules from complex mixtures. In alternative protein production, these technologies include
membrane filtration (micro, ultra, nano), centrifugal separation, chromatographic methods, and
precipitation techniques. They are essential for achieving food-grade purity levels.

Learn More
][25]
[
[Drying Technologies]

### Drying Technologies

Drying technologies convert wet protein products into stable powders or dried forms for storage,
transport, and further processing. Key methods include spray drying, freeze drying (lyophilization),
drum drying, and fluidized bed drying. The choice of drying method significantly impacts product
quality, functionality, and cost.

Learn More
][26]
[
[Extrusion Technologies]

### Extrusion Technologies

Extrusion technologies use mechanical energy, heat, and moisture to transform raw protein materials
into structured food products. Twin-screw and single-screw extruders are the workhorses of the
plant-based meat industry, producing both textured vegetable protein (TVP) and high-moisture meat
analogues (HMMA). Modern extrusion lines can achieve throughputs of several tons per hour.

Learn More
][27]
[
[Food Structuring Technologies]

### Food Structuring Technologies

Food structuring technologies create complex multi-component food architectures using methods like
3D food printing, electrospinning, and microencapsulation. These enable the creation of products
with precise control over texture, flavor distribution, and nutritional composition. 3D food
printing is particularly promising for creating whole-cut meat analogues with realistic marbling
patterns.

Learn More
][28]
[
[Bioprocess Automation]

### Bioprocess Automation

Bioprocess automation integrates sensors, actuators, SCADA systems, and AI/ML algorithms to monitor
and control biological production processes in real-time. In alternative protein manufacturing,
automation ensures consistent product quality, reduces human error, enables 24/7 operation, and
optimizes yield through predictive process control.

Learn More
][29]
[
[QA/QC & Food Safety]

### QA/QC & Food Safety

Quality Assurance/Quality Control and food safety technologies ensure that alternative protein
products meet regulatory standards and consumer expectations. This encompasses analytical testing
(composition, allergens, contaminants), process validation, traceability systems, and compliance
with regulations like FDA, EFSA, and local food safety authorities. As novel food products,
alternative proteins face heightened regulatory scrutiny.

Learn More
][30]

## SEARCH - CAS NO / Product Name / Chemical Name

We specialize in the supply of APIs and complex intermediates, covering metabolites, ADC toxins,

## [Intact Quality Management Policy][174]

BOC Sciences has established a complete quality management system and successively obtained ISO
9001, ISO22000, ISO 14001, and other international certifications base on 20+ years of continuous
technological innovation and experience accumulation.

We supply Raw Materials of Healthcare Products complying Kosher, HALAL certifications, GRAS
(Generally Recognized as Safe) status, we have also acquired a HACCP certification, which is a
global food hygiene management system. We implement quality management to every procedure from
production to operation activities such as raw materials, inventory, production, testing, sales,
verification, and training.

## [Certified Facilities and Advanced Equipment][175]

Our state-of-the-art FDA Certified Facilities are with fermentation capability of over 2,000,000
liters. We provide all in-house Upstream & Downstream Processes, Quality Control, Regulatory & Lab
Testing on-site.
* Workers: 200+
* R&D Center: 2200 sq.m
* Specialized product lines for pharmaceutical, food and cosmetic products
* 4 Manufacturing sites
* 40+ reactors of from 30-4000 L, 170+ reactors from 20 KL to 30 KL, 24+ reactors of >100 KL
* 2 Hydrogenation reactors (200 L, 4Mpa and 1000L, 4Mpa)

Canada as a global leader in food, feed and fuel. A…

## Report][137]

March 13, 2026 – The Canola Council of Canada’s (CCC) board of directors has named Kevin Wright as
chair. Wright is General Manager Great Lakes Region with ADM. Wright succeeds Tessa Ritter, who
completed her two-year term as chair. “On behalf of the board, I’d like to thank Tessa Ritter for
her service as our…

## [Farmer funding to drive innovation and strengthen canola production under Canola Agronomic
## Research Program in 2026][139]

March 4, 2026 – The three Prairie provincial canola grower associations have evaluated and selected
11 canola research projects to receive funding under the Canola Agronomic Research Program (CARP) in
2026. This investment includes over $2.4 million from Alberta Canola, SaskOilseeds and Manitoba
Canola Growers, as well as over $495,000 from the Western Grains Research Foundation…

# Transforming Waste, Powering the Future

[Screenshot 2025-05-05 082759.jpg]

Pioneering sustainable solutions for a greener future. Join us in our mission.

Learn More

## Our Story

## Our Mission

## At Circa Biotech, our mission is to revolutionize waste management and promote sustainability by
## transforming organic waste into valuable resources like sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), insect
## protein, and organic fertilizer. We aim to create a circular economy where waste is minimized,
## resources are optimized, and environmental stewardship is at the forefront.

[1e5fc53d-15cc-4331-a982-1fe830ca977c.png]

Founded in 2020, Circa Biotech is dedicated to transforming waste into valuable resources through
innovative engineering solutions.

## About

Meet the Managers

Together, Dr. Haythem Riahi and Dr. Liudmila Prozorova lead Circa Biotech with a shared vision of
creating a sustainable future. Their expertise and passion for environmental stewardship inspire our
team and community to pursue innovative and impactful solutions.

[About Us ][13]
* [[Facebook]][14]
* [[LinkedIn]][15]
* [[Instagram]][16]

## Behind Circa Biotech

Our Executive Managers

[KSST-HaythemLuidmila-2601_edited.jpg]

Chief Executive Officer

Dr. Haythem Riahi

Dr. Haythem Riahi brings over 20 years of expertise in biotechnology and B2B marketing. With a Ph.D.
in Biotechnology, Dr. Riahi has led numerous groundbreaking projects in sustainable waste management
and renewable energy. His visionary leadership and commitment to sustainability drive Circa
Biotech’s mission to transform organic waste into valuable resources. 
* [[LinkedIn]][17]

[KSST-HaythemLuidmila-2706_edited_edited.]

Chief Operating Officer

Dr. Liudmila Prozorova

Dr. Liudmila Prozorova, our Chief Operating Officer, has over 18 years of experience in supply chain
and project management. She holds a Ph.D. in Engineering and has a remarkable track record in
streamlining operations and enhancing efficiency. Dr. Prozorova's innovative approach ensures that
Circa Biotech’s processes are both effective and sustainable.
* [[LinkedIn]][18]

## Our Services

Insect Protein

We produce high-quality protein meal from BSFL, providing a sustainable and efficient alternative to
conventional protein sources like soy and fishmeal for animal feed.

Oil & Bio-diesel

We produce BSFL oil for SAF feedstock as a renewable energy source derived from larvae oil, offering
a low-carbon alternative to traditional jet fuels and helping the aviation industry meet its
sustainability goals.

Organic Fertiliser

Our organic fertilizer, derived from insect waste, enhances soil health, boosts crop yields, and
reduces the need for chemical fertilizers, promoting sustainable agriculture.

# Transforming Waste, Powering the Future

[Screenshot 2025-05-05 082759.jpg]

Pioneering sustainable solutions for a greener future. Join us in our mission.

Learn More

## Our Story

## Our Mission

## At Circa Biotech, our mission is to revolutionize waste management and promote sustainability by
## transforming organic waste into valuable resources like sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), insect
## protein, and organic fertilizer. We aim to create a circular economy where waste is minimized,
## resources are optimized, and environmental stewardship is at the forefront.

[1e5fc53d-15cc-4331-a982-1fe830ca977c.png]

Founded in 2020, Circa Biotech is dedicated to transforming waste into valuable resources through
innovative engineering solutions.

## About

Meet the Managers

Together, Dr. Haythem Riahi and Dr. Liudmila Prozorova lead Circa Biotech with a shared vision of
creating a sustainable future. Their expertise and passion for environmental stewardship inspire our
team and community to pursue innovative and impactful solutions.

[About Us ][13]

* [[LinkedIn]][15]
* [[Instagram]][16]

## Behind Circa Biotech

Our Executive Managers

[KSST-HaythemLuidmila-2601_edited.jpg]

Chief Executive Officer

Dr. Haythem Riahi

Dr. Haythem Riahi brings over 20 years of expertise in biotechnology and B2B marketing. With a Ph.D.
in Biotechnology, Dr. Riahi has led numerous groundbreaking projects in sustainable waste management
and renewable energy. His visionary leadership and commitment to sustainability drive Circa
Biotech’s mission to transform organic waste into valuable resources. 
* [[LinkedIn]][17]

[KSST-HaythemLuidmila-2706_edited_edited.]

Chief Operating Officer

Dr. Liudmila Prozorova

Dr. Liudmila Prozorova, our Chief Operating Officer, has over 18 years of experience in supply chain
and project management. She holds a Ph.D. in Engineering and has a remarkable track record in
streamlining operations and enhancing efficiency. Dr. Prozorova's innovative approach ensures that
Circa Biotech’s processes are both effective and sustainable.
* [[LinkedIn]][18]

## Our Services

Insect Protein

We produce high-quality protein meal from BSFL, providing a sustainable and efficient alternative to
conventional protein sources like soy and fishmeal for animal feed.

Oil & Bio-diesel

We produce BSFL oil for SAF feedstock as a renewable energy source derived from larvae oil, offering
a low-carbon alternative to traditional jet fuels and helping the aviation industry meet its
sustainability goals.

Organic Fertiliser

Our organic fertilizer, derived from insect waste, enhances soil health, boosts crop yields, and
reduces the need for chemical fertilizers, promoting sustainable agriculture.

# Reshaping our

# global food system,

# together.

## 
## The Unconventional Summit

The last two years have changed so much about who we are and how we interact with each other.
Before, we might have planned a large event with thousands of people mixing and sharing both
products and ideas. Instead, we’ve learned that a more intimate retreat gives all of us the
opportunity to deepen our connection to our goals in a more secure environment. 


Coming from all corners of the globe and all points in the food chain, our participants are a symbol
of the progress that can be achieved through collaboration and innovation. Their presence reminds us
that whatever challenge we face, we can always overcome. 

 

We’ve all changed, but our mission remains the same. To set the table for a radically different food
system through collaboration with industry leaders, activists, visionaries, and changemakers. 

 


[Read more][22]
[Image by Etienne Bösiger]

## Transformation begins with connections

[Mountain Range]

## It’s time to eat like the future
## depends on it.

The global food supply is more fragile than ever. Climate change, food waste, agricultural
practices, food security, and nutrition inequality have created a perfect storm of challenges that
we must now weather together. 

 

Solutions are emerging from all over the planet and companies are beginning to see the importance of
shifting their focus to sustainability. The more they collaborate, the bigger their impact. 

 

Edible Planet is the ecosystem that connects voices and visions to develop the global food
infrastructure we need for a resilient and productive world.

[Meet the Ecosystem][23]
[TEDX][24]

### A holistic platform where business leaders, policy makers, startups, and entrepreneurs can
### connect and exchange resources, knowledge, and support for new ideas in the global food

### DEVELOP

[Dark Ocean]

### New voices and underrepresented groups in the global effort to create a more equitable food
### system

### EMPOWER

[Sunrise%2520over%2520the%2520Wheat%2520F]

### A shared comprehensive global database of stakeholders and problem solving tools that is
### accessible to all partners

### BUILD

[Image by Olena Sergienko]

### Original, dynamic written, visual and digital content that informs and educates about the
### challenges and solutions possible within the global food chain

### CREATE

### The food system through collaboration and encouraged synergy between individuals, organizations,
### companies and institutions

### TRANSFORM

As experts in agrifood innovation, Edible Planet Ventures manages a range of operations to help
companies re-define their strategies to stay ahead of the curve. 

 

We bring a global ecosystem of stakeholders, collaborators and resources along with extensive
experience in the global food sector to help your business succeed.

[Get Started][25]

## Are you ready to Accelerate Your Business?

[Image by Mark Timberlake]

## the more we share,
##    the more we learn,
##       the more we transform.

It's time to come together and to use all of the tools we have at hand to think of new solutions to
our global challenges. The Encounter is a platform for sharing knowledge, ideas and solutions. With
a newswire, podcast, blog series, and events the Encounter is built on multimedia formats that
utilize the greatest strength we have. Our humanity.

[The Encounter][26]

## Check it Out!

## FOOD TECH JUNKIES

#### Check it out NOW!

A deep dive podcast series for anyone who is passionate about food innovation

[Listen Now][27]

[Info@edibleplanetventures.com][28]

[Summit][30]

## The Unconventional Summit

The last two years have changed so much about who we are and how we interact with each other.
Before, we might have planned a large event with thousands of people mixing and sharing both
products and ideas. Instead, we’ve learned that a more intimate retreat gives all of us the
opportunity to deepen our connection to our goals in a more secure environment. 


Coming from all corners of the globe and all points in the food chain, our participants are a symbol
of the progress that can be achieved through collaboration and innovation. Their presence reminds us
that whatever challenge we face, we can always overcome. 

 

We’ve all changed, but our mission remains the same. To set the table for a radically different food
system through collaboration with industry leaders, activists, visionaries, and changemakers. 

 


[Read more][22]
[Image by Etienne Bösiger]

## Transformation begins with connections

## It’s time to eat like the future

The global food supply is more fragile than ever. Climate change, food waste, agricultural
practices, food security, and nutrition inequality have created a perfect storm of challenges that
we must now weather together. 

 

Solutions are emerging from all over the planet and companies are beginning to see the importance of
shifting their focus to sustainability. The more they collaborate, the bigger their impact. 

 

Edible Planet is the ecosystem that connects voices and visions to develop the global food
infrastructure we need for a resilient and productive world.

Adherent Cell and Derivatives Specialists

# Esco Healthcare
# Product Portfolio

The Esco Healthcare has a wide range of bioprocess solutions from adherent bioreactors, stirred tank
bioreactors, consumables, cell-line specific culture medium, and more. Bioprocess manufacturing
includes several key components to improve product yield. As part of the bioprocess equipment
manufacturers worldwide, our systems are perfect for research and development up to commercial or
manufacturing scale.

CelCradle

CelCradle is a bench-scale bioreactor system that can support high adherent cell density culture. It
is a single-use, cost effective packed-bed bioreactor system for adherent scale-up from laboratory
scale to production scale. This disposable bioreactor fits inside a 6ft³ CO2 incubator (for batch
culture) or 8.5ft³ CO2 incubator (for perfusion culture).

The ready-to-use bottles, as part of single-use manufacturing, helps eliminate validation costs as
compared to multiple-use system when starting on your next cell culture run. The system components
come pre-sterilized, pre-packed that speed up your research whether for vaccine, stem cell, or viral
production applications.

[Learn More ][9]
[CelCradle]

TideXcell

TideXcell^{®} is a linearly scalable pilot bioreactor system that runs on Tide Motion principle. It
is ideal for biomass expansion of adherent cells under single-use or multiple-use technologies. The
pilot scale bioreactor is also integrated with desirable and advanced features such as pH and DO
(Dissolved Oxygen) measurement capability, Siemens HMI or PLC-based monitoring and control system,
compressed air path that comes with a double HEPA and VOC (volatile organic chemicals) filters as
well as other accessories.
[Learn More ][10]
[TideXcell]

## Imagining Tide from a 360 perspective is now ready for viewing!

With iTide, our newest and latest bioreactors in the pipeline are perfectly curated to provide
real-time user experience. One can see how the Tide Motion works for every system, its culture
features, footprint, and many more.

Let your eyes take in a visual representation of both bench-scale and closed, automated
manufacturing scale bioreactor system for cell culture with just the tip of your cursor.

[The Other Tide  ][11]
WHO WE ARE

Esco Healthcare is a division of Esco LifeSciences group that provides bioprocess solutions. We
market bioprocessing tools such as bioreactors for both adherent and suspension culture, harvesting
systems for a closed, automated product harvest, and more.

[Learn More About Us  ][12]

Adherent Cell and Derivatives Specialists

# Esco Healthcare
# Product Portfolio

The Esco Healthcare has a wide range of bioprocess solutions from adherent bioreactors, stirred tank
bioreactors, consumables, cell-line specific culture medium, and more. Bioprocess manufacturing
includes several key components to improve product yield. As part of the bioprocess equipment
manufacturers worldwide, our systems are perfect for research and development up to commercial or
manufacturing scale.

CelCradle

CelCradle is a bench-scale bioreactor system that can support high adherent cell density culture. It
is a single-use, cost effective packed-bed bioreactor system for adherent scale-up from laboratory
scale to production scale. This disposable bioreactor fits inside a 6ft³ CO2 incubator (for batch
culture) or 8.5ft³ CO2 incubator (for perfusion culture).

The ready-to-use bottles, as part of single-use manufacturing, helps eliminate validation costs as
compared to multiple-use system when starting on your next cell culture run. The system components
come pre-sterilized, pre-packed that speed up your research whether for vaccine, stem cell, or viral
production applications.

[Learn More ][9]
[CelCradle]

TideXcell

TideXcell^{®} is a linearly scalable pilot bioreactor system that runs on Tide Motion principle. It
is ideal for biomass expansion of adherent cells under single-use or multiple-use technologies. The
pilot scale bioreactor is also integrated with desirable and advanced features such as pH and DO
(Dissolved Oxygen) measurement capability, Siemens HMI or PLC-based monitoring and control system,
compressed air path that comes with a double HEPA and VOC (volatile organic chemicals) filters as
well as other accessories.
[Learn More ][10]
[TideXcell]

## Imagining Tide from a 360 perspective is now ready for viewing!

With iTide, our newest and latest bioreactors in the pipeline are perfectly curated to provide
real-time user experience. One can see how the Tide Motion works for every system, its culture
features, footprint, and many more.

Let your eyes take in a visual representation of both bench-scale and closed, automated
manufacturing scale bioreactor system for cell culture with just the tip of your cursor.

[The Other Tide  ][11]
WHO WE ARE

Esco Healthcare is a division of Esco LifeSciences group that provides bioprocess solutions. We
market bioprocessing tools such as bioreactors for both adherent and suspension culture, harvesting
systems for a closed, automated product harvest, and more.

#### Tools & Benchmarks

Our tools provide detailed analysis on material investment risks and opportunities in the animal
agriculture sector. Whether through our flagship Protein Producer Index, our cutting-edge Climate
Risk Tool or our informative Alternative Protein Framework, investor members can rely on FAIRR for
relevant insights.

[Button-Arrow-Inactive]
][3]

#### Investor Engagements

We facilitate opportunities for investors to engage in dialogues with companies in the agri-food
sector around material risks and opportunities. In addition, we provide our investor members with
detailed research and analysis on the long-term business resilience and sustainable value of
corporates across the food system supply chain.

[Button-Arrow-Inactive]
][4]
[

#### Policy Action

We engage with governments, regulators, and industry bodies to create awareness of systemic risks
linked to intensive animal farming practices. With the support and on behalf of investor members, we
produce statements highlighting investor expectations to build and support the transition of a more
sustainable food system.

[Button-Arrow-Inactive]

Our thought leadership reports and insights enable investor members to deepen their understanding of
material issues that impact global food systems and portfolio companies exposed to the sector. We
produce state-of-industry and outlook reports across relevant themes, underlining their materiality
and providing a view on how to tackle the negative impacts of current food systems.

## Why forestreet exists

The procurement function developed in a world where the supply base evolved slowly: “Reliability”,
“Optimization”, “Marginal Gains”. The pattern has changed. Shocks, of one kind or another, seem to
be here to stay. Procurement need to retool to be agile, global, adaptable. 

Forestreet is a vendor and market discovery software that maps out suppliers, on demand, in any
geography and category combination. It provides high-quality context and insights, making category
managers multi-lingual experts with global perspective and local knowledge. It is a force-multiplier
of the precious time procurement professionals invest in researching and updating categories. 

## OUR PLATFORM

### Forestreet puts the power in your hands

With our AI-powered platform you can search across millions of potential vendors in seconds, index
and enrich the data and instantly create a curated list of companies and products based on your
specific criteria. It isn’t skewed by sponsored content, blunt categorizations and it isn’t limited
by the supplier lists recycled from other clients. So you capture everything, not just the companies
with the biggest marketing budgets. 

Categorise the market as you see it, search relevant news articles, access high-quality analytics
and auto-generate high quality reports. All in one intuitive platform.

[ Discover our Solutions ][46]

## A NEW AGE OF SUPPLIER INTELLIGENCE

### Search as it should be

Currently, search is optimised for sellers: there is too much information and too many ways for
companies to game searches and buy their way to the top of results. Despite these serious problems,
even top analyst firms rely heavily on Google to research and create reports.
But this is no longer your only option. Forestreet clears a path straight to the information that’s
useful to you. Why wait weeks for a consultancy report? Become a market expert in minutes with our
AI-powered SaaS platform.

## WHY FORESTREET

#### Forestreet gives you research superpowers

Forestreet’s AI platform augments your expertise, to deliver high-quality research at pace.

### Hyper speed

Fancy being able to read, analyse and index thousands of webpages in seconds? Collect all the key
data points about revenue, funding and company location without lifting a finger? Our AI tool
supercharges the whole research process, making impossible feats simple.

### Super flexibility

Our powerful platform lets you iterate and learn as you go, adapting agilely to market fluctuations
and changing business needs. Before you know it you’ll be pivoting and lunging across markets with a
newly unleashed suppleness.

### 360° enhanced vision

Don’t settle for patchy market overviews and foggy guesswork. Our AI platform gives you a clear view
of the whole market in one glance, magnifying trends and insights which are otherwise a speck in the
distance.

### Omniscience

Well, not quite. But with an inexhaustible supply of information at your fingertips, compared to
everyone else in the meeting, you’ll feel pretty all-knowing.

## NEWS & INSIGHTS

Our latest news and insights from the Forestreet team

be here to stay. Procurement need to retool to be agile, global, adaptable. 

Forestreet is a vendor and market discovery software that maps out suppliers, on demand, in any
geography and category combination. It provides high-quality context and insights, making category
managers multi-lingual experts with global perspective and local knowledge. It is a force-multiplier
of the precious time procurement professionals invest in researching and updating categories.

### Forestreet puts the power in your hands

With our AI-powered platform you can search across millions of potential vendors in seconds, index
and enrich the data and instantly create a curated list of companies and products based on your
specific criteria. It isn’t skewed by sponsored content, blunt categorizations and it isn’t limited
by the supplier lists recycled from other clients. So you capture everything, not just the companies
with the biggest marketing budgets. 

Categorise the market as you see it, search relevant news articles, access high-quality analytics
and auto-generate high quality reports. All in one intuitive platform.

planes, trucks, cars, trains and ships on Earth.

with farming animals – enabling people to eat familiar foods they already enjoy and want without

[PHOTO OF A PREY BIRD AT GAMLA NATURE RESERVE IN THE GLOAN HEIGHTS.]Credit: Avi Ohayon, Israel
Government Press Office

emerging zoonotic diseases—viruses that jump from animal hosts to humans and are capable of

antimicrobial resistance that could spell the end of modern medicine. By 2050, it is estimated that

trillion][66].

reduce the risk of developing heart disease. In August 2020, [researchers found][67] that in
comparison to animal-based meat, consuming plant-based meat products led to statistically
significant positive impacts on cholesterol, weight, and heart disease markers among the study’s
participants.

pandemics as they are free of antibiotics and fecal contamination and involve no risk of zoonotic
diseases. While more research and innovation are needed to continue improving nutritional profiles
and human health benefits, alternative proteins provide an opportunity to bring a healthy change in
how we produce what we eat.

the price of grains and legumes and entrenching global poverty. According to the World Resources
Institute, it takes [nine calories of feed][68] to produce one calorie of chicken meat.

it with a system as inefficient as animal agriculture.

crops to feed people instead of animals, creating a more efficient and just food system.

## Israel: A leader in alternative proteins innovation

[Israel is ranked as one of the world’s most innovative countries][70] and is [number one in the
world for per-capita startups][71]. It is a truly creative R&D powerhouse thanks to its high
concentration of talented researchers and entrepreneurs and its supportive regulatory and business
environment and infrastructure.

Israel continues to lead as a global hub for alternative proteins, with over US$1.3 billion in
venture capital funding to date, second only to the United States in alternative protein investments
worldwide. Israel is home to over 75 alternative protein startups, breaking records in 2023 with 15
new startups founded and six new production facilities launched.

This is in large part thanks to Israel’s thriving academic ecosystem, with over 70 active
alternative protein researchers across 11 academic institutions, and two dedicated food tech
research centers announced. The government also provides critical support for alternative proteins,
including funding for research grants, startups, and workforce training, and promotes a supportive
regulatory framework.

GFI Israel works as a catalyst for the entire sector, leveraging the Israeli entrepreneurial
mentality and partnering with forward-thinking scientists, businesses, and policymakers to ensure
the country continues to advance solutions for local and global food and climate challenges and
drives a thriving economy. The innovations that continue to come out of Israel put us on the path
toward the global transition that is so necessary.

Institute, it takes [nine calories of feed][68] to produce one calorie of chicken meat.

By 2050, the world will have to feed a population of [nearly 10 billion people][69], and we can’t do
it with a system as inefficient as animal agriculture.

By making meat directly from plants and cultivating it directly from cells, we can focus on growing
crops to feed people instead of animals, creating a more efficient and just food system.

[Photo of apples from the Golan Heights.]Credit: Mark Neyman, Israel Government Press Office

## Israel: A leader in alternative proteins innovation

[Israel is ranked as one of the world’s most innovative countries][70] and is [number one in the
world for per-capita startups][71]. It is a truly creative R&D powerhouse thanks to its high
concentration of talented researchers and entrepreneurs and its supportive regulatory and business
environment and infrastructure.

Israel continues to lead as a global hub for alternative proteins, with over US$1.3 billion in
venture capital funding to date, second only to the United States in alternative protein investments
worldwide. Israel is home to over 75 alternative protein startups, breaking records in 2023 with 15
new startups founded and six new production facilities launched.

This is in large part thanks to Israel’s thriving academic ecosystem, with over 70 active
alternative protein researchers across 11 academic institutions, and two dedicated food tech
research centers announced. The government also provides critical support for alternative proteins,
including funding for research grants, startups, and workforce training, and promotes a supportive
regulatory framework.

GFI Israel works as a catalyst for the entire sector, leveraging the Israeli entrepreneurial
mentality and partnering with forward-thinking scientists, businesses, and policymakers to ensure
the country continues to advance solutions for local and global food and climate challenges and
drives a thriving economy. The innovations that continue to come out of Israel put us on the path
toward the global transition that is so necessary.

sustainable, secure, and just protein supply. We identify the most effective solutions, advance
open-access research, bring new talent to the field, and empower partners.

[][21]
[Solutions database][22]

Explore startup ideas, commercial opportunities, research projects, and investment priorities
throughout the alternative protein supply chain.

[**2023 APAC State of the Industry Report**][23]

This comprehensive analysis covers public-private investments, the R&D and startup ecosystems,
product development and launch, and key market insights.

[][24]
[Initiatives][25]

Learn about GFI’s open-access research, policy work, and other alt protein programmes—all powered by
donors.

[][26]
[GFIdeas community][27]

GFIdeas is a community for entrepreneurs, investors, scientists, and government and corporate
representatives who are driving alternative protein innovation globally.

[][28]
[Alternative protein career pathways][29]

Find your path in the booming alternative protein sector using our interactive career guide, which
equips you with job archetypes and descriptions, skills requirements, and local and global training
programmes to excel in sustainable food production.

[Fuel the future of food][30]

## Taking good food global

Our food system is global. Our biggest challenges are global. Our solutions must be global as well.
* [Overview][31]
* [GFI Brazil][32]
* [GFI Europe][33]
* [GFI India][34]
* [GFI Israel][35]
* [GFI US][36]
* [GFI Japan][37]

[Overview][38]

### **GFI around the world**

GFI is an international network of nonprofits strategically positioned to have the greatest possible
impact on the global food system. These countries and regions have robust scientific ecosystems and
governments that are committed to using innovation to solve global problems. In addition to GFI
APAC, our network operates in six additional countries and regions: Brazil, Europe, India, Israel,
Japan, and the United States.

[GFI Brazil][39]

### GFI Brazil

GFI Brazil is focused on advancing alternative proteins in Brazil, which boasts world-class
agricultural universities working to efficiently feed the world, as well as a government and
corporations committed to identifying the potential of native species. 

[Group photo of GFI Brazil employees]
[Visit Brazil][40]
[GFI Europe][41]

### GFI Europe

GFI Europe is focused on advancing alternative proteins in Europe, which is home to much of the
world’s scientific and commercial talent, and is one of the biggest potential markets for
plant-based and cultivated meat.

[Group shot of GFI Europe employees]©Barbara Evripidou/FirstAvenuePhotography.com
[Visit Europe][42]
[GFI India][43]

### GFI India

GFI India is the central expert organization, thought leader, and convening body in the Indian
“alternative protein” or “smart protein” sector, accelerating this ecosystem in a nation on the cusp
of becoming the world’s most populous. India has world-class scientific institutions and a
government committed to using alternative proteins to address malnutrition and to spark robust
economic growth.

[Visit India][44]
[GFI Israel][45]

### GFI Israel

The Good Food Institute Israel (GFI Israel) is a nonprofit think tank, working to harness the power
of local alternative protein research and innovation to target the world’s climate, global health,
food security, and biodiversity goals. As a catalyst for the entire sector, GFI Israel leverages the
Israeli entrepreneurial mentality and partners with forward-thinking scientists, businesses, and
policymakers to advance research and industry breakthroughs, and promote governmental support for
alternative proteins.

[Group photo of GFI Israel employees]
[Visit Israel][46]
[GFI US][47]

### GFI US

Founded in 2016, GFI US is on a mission to identify the most effective solutions, mobilize resources
and talent, and empower partners across the food system to make alternative proteins accessible,
affordable, and delicious.

[Photo of GFI US employees at a retreat, giving each other high fives]
[Visit US][48]
[GFI Japan][49]

### GFI Japan

The Good Food Institute Japan (GFI Japan) is a nonprofit think tank working to make the global food
system better for the planet, people, and animals. Alongside scientists, businesses, and
policymakers, GFI Japan’s teams focus on making plant-based and cultivated meat delicious,
affordable, and accessible.

[Visit Japan][50]

# Golden is now part of *ComplyAdvantage.*

We set out to build a self-constructing knowledge graph of the world's information. In 2024, that
technology found its home inside ComplyAdvantage — powering financial crime intelligence for over
1,000 enterprises.

The acquisition

## Acquired by ComplyAdvantage in 2024.

On 24 April 2024, ComplyAdvantage — the AI-driven financial crime intelligence firm protecting over
1,000 enterprises across 75 countries — acquired Golden.

01

### Into the ingestion layer

Golden's data extraction and entity-disambiguation methods now feed ComplyAdvantage's ingestion
pipeline, sharpening real-time risk insights for regulated institutions.

02

### Two teams, united

Golden's AI and large-language-model specialists joined ComplyAdvantage's data science team to build
on interconnected data at scale.

03

### Founder as advisor

Founder and CEO Jude Gomila joined ComplyAdvantage as a board observer and special advisor. a16z
became a top shareholder of the combined company.

"Financial crime insights built on *interconnected data* have been our north star."
[Visit ComplyAdvantage →][5]
The story

## A self-constructing knowledge base.

Golden set out to map human knowledge with machine intelligence — automating one of the world's
largest knowledge graphs from millions of disparate sources.

Founded · 2017 Golden

Jude Gomila starts Golden in San Francisco to combine artificial and human intelligence into one
continuously reconciled record.

Seed · 2019 $5M

a16z, Founders Fund, Gigafund and SV Angel back the first self-constructing knowledge database.

Series A · 2021 $14.5M

Led by a16z; Marc Andreessen joins the board. Golden closes a $1M US Air Force contract.

Series B · 2022 $40M

a16z leads again to scale the graph, bringing Golden's total funding to roughly $59.5M.

Acquired · 2024 ComplyAdvantage

Golden joins ComplyAdvantage to power AI-enriched financial crime intelligence worldwide.

The team

## Founder, engineers, and the investors behind them.

Golden was founded by Jude Gomila — a Cambridge engineer who previously co-founded the mobile
platform Heyzap (acquired 2016) — and built by a small team of AI, NLP and knowledge-graph
specialists.

Founder & CEO Jude Gomila

Set the mission of mapping the world's knowledge; now board observer and special advisor at
ComplyAdvantage.

Lead investor a16z

Andreessen Horowitz backed every round; Marc Andreessen served on Golden's board.

Backers Founders Fund

With Gigafund, SV Angel, DCVC and angels — roughly $59.5M raised across seed, Series A and Series B.

The team AI & NLP

Engineers specialising in data extraction, entity disambiguation and large language models — now
part of ComplyAdvantage's data science team.

[GOLDEN.com][6]

A self-constructing knowledge graph founded in San Francisco in 2017. Acquired by ComplyAdvantage in
2024.

## **Future-proofing Europe’s food system**

People across Europe want a sustainable, secure and just food system. European governments have set
some of the world’s most ambitious targets for reducing emissions and farming in harmony with nature
– and diversifying our protein supply will be essential to achieve them. We know our current food
system needs to change – but we don’t want to give up our favourite foods.

Taste, price and accessibility are non-negotiable for most of us when we’re deciding what to eat –
but right now, the most sustainable options aren’t meeting those needs.

So at the Good Food Institute Europe, we champion the science, policies and investment needed to
make alternative proteins delicious, affordable and accessible.

By diversifying Europe’s protein supply to include options like plant-based and cultivated meat, we
can keep eating our favourite foods while boosting food security, meeting our climate targets and
supporting nature-friendly farming.

## **What are alternative proteins?**

[Juicy Marbles steak Ramen]Photo: Juicy Marbles
[Plant-based][125]
Photo: Mosa Meat
[Cultivated][126]

[Fermentation][128]

## **The potential of protein diversification**

### Boosting food security

Recent global shocks have shown the pressing need to strengthen the resilience of agrifood supply
chains, and increase Europe’s food sovereignty. 

[regenerative farming practices with a cover crop]

Global demand for meat is projected to[ grow by at least 52%][129] by 2050, and in Europe we already
feed [45% of all the crops we produce][130] to animals and use half of our farmland for animal
agriculture. The EU is also the world’s [second-largest importer of seafood][131] – depending on
other regions for more than two-thirds of the seafood Europeans eat. In an increasingly uncertain
world, we need a more sustainable system.

Plant-based and cultivated meat could deliver the meat people want with up to [90% less land][132],
and fermentation can make nutritious food from crops that would otherwise go to waste. Even a modest
diversification of protein production could enable [21% of European domestic farmland][133] to
transition to agroecological farming, or be used to boost domestic food production or restore
natural habitats.

### Strengthening economies

Protein diversification can drive green growth and create highly skilled jobs. Europe is well-placed
to reap these economic benefits, which – [with significant public investment][134] – could add over
€900 billion to the global economy and create 10 million jobs by 2050. 

[two workers in the food sector]

For countries willing to invest, alternative proteins could pay major dividends. According to
[AgriFoodTure][135], Denmark could create 27,000 jobs in the plant-based sector, and add up to 13
billion kroner (€1.7 billion) to the Danish economy, with just a small fraction of the growing
global market. [Research by Green Alliance][136] has found that the UK alternative proteins industry
could be worth up to £6.8 billion per year and create 25,000 jobs by 2035. 

Europe is currently the [world’s biggest market][137] for plant-based meat, and was the birthplace
of cultivated meat. Home to some of the field’s most innovative scientists and startups, we have the
potential to lead the world on alternative proteins. But as countries like the [United States][138]
and [China][139] begin to invest, Europe risks falling behind as it did with solar energy.
Governments must invest now to realise the economic benefits of alternative proteins.

### Reducing climate emissions

[Research by Oxford University][140] shows that the world cannot meet its climate targets without
shifting away from conventional animal agriculture. But in Europe, [meat consumption is
increasing][141].

Animal agriculture causes [20% of global greenhouse gas emissions][142] – [equivalent to][143] all

habitats to ensure food production works hand in hand with nature. But we simply don’t have enough

[Image of a frog flourishing on a nature-friendly farm]

diversification of protein production could at least double the share of organically farmed land
across 10 European countries.

Farmers will also play a key role in a diversified protein supply chain – producing high-quality and
sustainable ingredients, and diversifying Europe’s crops to improve nutrition, reduce monocultures
and safeguard local production. By putting the right policies, incentives and structures in place,
European governments can help farmers to seize these opportunities.

Diversifying Europe’s protein supply is essential if governments are to address global public health
challenges such as diet-related ill health, climate change, antimicrobial resistance and pandemic

## **Future-proofing Europe’s food system**

People across Europe want a sustainable, secure and just food system. European governments have set
some of the world’s most ambitious targets for reducing emissions and farming in harmony with nature

system needs to change – but we don’t want to give up our favourite foods.

Taste, price and accessibility are non-negotiable for most of us when we’re deciding what to eat –
but right now, the most sustainable options aren’t meeting those needs.

So at the Good Food Institute Europe, we champion the science, policies and investment needed to
make alternative proteins delicious, affordable and accessible.

By diversifying Europe’s protein supply to include options like plant-based and cultivated meat, we
can keep eating our favourite foods while boosting food security, meeting our climate targets and
supporting nature-friendly farming.

Plant-based and cultivated meat could deliver the meat people want with up to [90% less land][132],
